scenarios.title: Video Session
scenarios.text: The analyst catches you on your way out of training, laptop under one arm. "Twenty minutes on {opponent}? Their full-back pushes up and leaves a gap. I can show you exactly where."

outcomes.text: By the end you could draw their back line from memory. Word gets back to {manager} that you stayed.

choices.text: "Send me the clips. I'll watch at home."

outcomes.text: You watch them on the bus, twice. Fair enough.
The clips sit unopened on your phone all week.
Two of you, one laptop, too many jokes, but you both leave knowing the plan.

scenarios.title: Extra Shift
scenarios.text: Training's over. Everyone heads for the showers, but the pitch is still lit and there's a bag of balls by the goal.

outcomes.text: Fifty shots, left foot then right. The last ten all go in.
Your legs are heavy the next morning. The fitness coach is not impressed.
An early night. You wake up feeling sharp.

scenarios.title: The Group Chat
scenarios.text: Your phone keeps buzzing. Half the squad is planning a night out, two days before {opponent}. "You coming, {first}?"

outcomes.text: One drink, a lot of laughing, home by ten. The lads respect it.
Someone posts a photo. {manager} sees it. Nobody gets dropped, but there's a look at training.
A few eye-roll emojis. You sleep well.
It catches on. Twelve of you squeeze into a small restaurant near the ground.

scenarios.title: A Few Questions
scenarios.text: A reporter from the local paper is waiting by the car park. "Quick one, {first}. What do you make of {opponent}?"

outcomes.text: Boring, but safe. The club's media officer gives you a thumbs up.
It makes the back page. The dressing room loves it.
It ends up pinned to their dressing room wall. {manager} asks you to keep quiet next time.
No story, no trouble.

scenarios.title: A Small Deal
scenarios.text: A small boot brand messages you. They'll pay 60 for one post wearing their new pair. The boots look a bit cheap.

outcomes.text: One photo, one caption, 60 in your account.
The teammates won't stop calling you "the model" all week.
You'd rather your football did the talking.

scenarios.title: A Call From Home
scenarios.text: It's your mum. Everyone back in {city} is following the results, and your little cousin wants a shirt with {shirt} on the back.

outcomes.text: A photo arrives a week later: your cousin in the shirt, grinning, three sizes too big.
You hang up feeling lighter than you have in weeks.
You feel a little guilty all evening.

scenarios.title: A Tight Hamstring
scenarios.text: Late in training, something pulls at the back of your thigh. It's probably nothing. Probably.

outcomes.text: Just tightness. A massage and some stretches, and you're cleared for {opponent}.
The physio wants you to rest a day. You hate it, but it's the right call.
It eases off by the morning. You got away with it.
It's worse the next day, and the staff work out you hid it. {manager} is not pleased.

scenarios.title: A Word From the Captain
scenarios.text: The captain sits down next to you in the canteen. "You've got something, {first}. But you drift out of games. Want some advice?"

outcomes.text: Twenty minutes on movement, talking and when to rest on the ball. You write it all down later.
A shrug. "Suit yourself." The captain doesn't offer again.
"Their number six is slow on the turn. Run at him." Noted.
